description:
## [0.22.4](https://github.com/Forsigh/waze-patches/compare/v0.22.2...v0.22.4) (2026-10-13)

### 🗑️ Removed

* **Map theme** and **OLED dark mode** are removed. Both rewrote Waze's map skin inside the APK; on-device
  testing showed the app breaking with them - the OLED black swallowed the map contents and the theme
  selector broke the map - so the full skin-rewrite approach is retired with them. The skin files ship
  stock again, and the versionCode refresh now waits for the mood artwork *and* the AMOLED row below -
  a minimal, night-only rebuild of the same idea, informed by the first attempt's post-mortem

### ✨ New patch

* **Morphe YouTube Music as a Waze audio partner** replaces "Add your own media apps as Waze audio
  partners": a direct port of Loupric/morphe-waze-music-patch (GPLv3, release v1.0.2, credited in the
  README and the source). The package is declared in Waze's manifest `<queries>` - without it Android's
  package visibility hides it from Waze entirely - and inserted into `SdkConfiguration.appConfigs` when
  `updateAppList` rebuilds the roster: upstream's `containsKey`-guarded block right after the scope save,
  built with the five-argument `au` constructor and feature bits `0x200001`
* the custom machinery is retired rather than kept alongside: the `partners` / `alsoAllowPackage` /
  `mediaBrowserAction` / `allowAllPackages` options, the `au.g` availability override and the audio-SDK
  config forcing are all gone. On-device testing under the previous build did not produce a working
  partner, and upstream's exact pair is what its own users run
* the row is on by default, exactly as upstream lists it
* **AMOLED dark mode** (opt-in, off by default) - the second, informed attempt at the AMOLED night map:
  night skin files only, the canvas becomes true black (`#000000`) and the nine road families are lifted
  15% toward white (the first attempt used 10%) so they keep their contrast against it. Day mode, labels,
  traffic and route colours stay stock, and the day files are asserted byte-identical. Two measured facts
  from the first attempt's post-mortem shape it: `map_background` is also the render tree's "eraser"
  colour (referenced ~20 times as feature strokes), so the black cascades by design to match the canvas,
  and the higher lift compensates the dark-on-dark night palette. Applied at patch time; nothing injected
* **Disable Play Store updates** (opt-in, off by default) - a port of Morphe's universal patch of the same
  name (`MorpheApp/morphe-patches`, GPLv3, credited): the manifest version code is locked above Play's
  2,100,000,000 ceiling, so the store always sees the installed copy as newer and never offers or applies
  an update. Two deliberate Waze adaptations: the locked value is `2,100,000,000 + minutes since 2026`
  rather than a frozen maximum, because Waze re-extracts its skins only when the versionCode *changes* -
  frozen, it would silently freeze every future skin edit; and instead of upstream's rewrite-everything
  preserve, only Waze's own package-version accessor (`com.waze.utils.n.a`, the push module's source) is
  made to report the pre-lock code, while the two extraction gates keep seeing the change. The manifest
  write runs in the resource half's `finalize`, so the lock is the last word on the number regardless of
  selection order
* the descriptions Morphe and the README show for every patch got a plain-language pass, and the credits
  section now lists only sources whose work actually ships in the bundle

patches.name: AMOLED dark mode
patches.description: Replaces Waze's stock night map with an AMOLED one: the map canvas becomes true black (#000000) and the nine road families are lifted 15% toward white so they keep their contrast against it. Only the night skins change - day mode, labels, traffic and route colours stay as Waze ships them. Applied at patch time: no runtime switch, nothing injected.

patches.name: Allow high refresh rate
patches.description: Waze rejects any display mode above 60 Hz when it picks the mode for its surface, so a 120 Hz screen is served 60 Hz. This raises that ceiling to the requested rate (120 Hz by default). Costs battery and heat - off by default.

options.description: The ceiling Waze accepts when choosing a display mode. 120 suits most modern panels; 90 or 60 to back off if the phone throttles.

patches.name: Auto zoom
patches.description: Keeps the auto-zoom mode you pick (no / yes / speed) from being overwritten when Waze syncs its server config. The setting comes from Waze itself; this makes it stick.

options.description: speed = zoom out progressively with speed, yes = always on, no = off.

patches.name: Average-speed camera alerts
patches.description: Turns on average-speed camera alerts and the recommended speed for the zone.

patches.name: Brief voice guidance
patches.description: Enables Waze's brief voice-guidance mode, which trims the spoken directions down.

patches.name: Disable Play Store updates
patches.description: Stops the Play Store from offering or applying updates to Waze: the manifest version code is locked above Play's maximum (2,100,000,000 + minutes), so the store always sees the installed copy as newer than its listing. The value advances on every re-patch, so Waze still refreshes its extracted resources, and Waze's own package-version accessor keeps reporting the pre-lock code. Ported from Morphe's universal "Disable Play Store updates" (GPLv3).

patches.name: Enable police & enforcement alerts
patches.description: Turns on Waze's police and enforcement alerts.

patches.name: Extended police & hazard alert distances
patches.description: Alerts for police, accidents and heavy traffic fire earlier, with their pre-alert distances extended.

patches.name: Lane guidance
patches.description: Turns on lane guidance, including the continue-straight hints.

patches.name: Morphe YouTube Music as a Waze audio partner
patches.description: Makes Morphe YouTube Music (app.morphe.android.apps.youtube.music) usable as Waze's audio partner: the package is declared in Waze's manifest so Android's package visibility lets Waze see it, and it is added to the audio-partner table (SdkConfiguration.appConfigs) whenever Waze rebuilds that roster. Ported from Loupric/morphe-waze-music-patch (GPLv3).

patches.name: Radar sound at any speed
patches.description: Plays the speed-camera alert sound even when you are not over the limit. Waze normally only sounds it when you are.

patches.name: Remove ads
patches.description: Forces Waze's advertising settings off, so the ad slots that respect those values stay empty.

patches.name: Show all cameras & road hazards
patches.description: Draws speed cameras, red-light cameras and speed bumps on the map, with their on-route notifications enabled.

patches.name: Speed limit sign always shown
patches.description: The speed-limit sign stays on the map, and its manual overrides become available.

patches.name: Speed-limit decrease warnings
patches.description: Warns when the posted speed limit drops, with a longer pre-alert distance than stock.

patches.name: Speedometer always on
patches.description: The speedometer stays on screen at any speed, including when stopped. Waze hides it below its own minimum speed otherwise.

patches.name: Unlock driver moods
patches.description: Waze's mood picker is gated three ways: an eligibility check that accepts only one mood name (and reads the beta-moods flag), a baby-account gate that hides moods, and a filtered native catalogue call. This opens all three, so moods already in the local catalogue - including special and hidden entries - become selectable. Artwork Waze has never downloaded is not invented.
